title: Tongues and colors
hook: the diversity of your languages and colors is among His signs (30:22)

segments.voice: Yesterday: mawadda and rahma, love and mercy placed between two people. Your line was love and mercy between.

Stand in the courtyard of the Great Mosque in Mecca at any hour, and listen. Indonesian, Urdu, Turkish, Hausa, Bosnian, Malay, Bengali, Somali, French, English, Arabic in a dozen accents. Faces of every shade, from every continent, walking the same circle, many in the same white cloth. Some pilgrims come home talking less about the buildings than about the crowd. The verse right after yesterday's has a word for what they saw.

Pickthall: "And of His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the difference of your languages and colours. Lo! herein indeed are portents for men of knowledge." Look at the company the verse keeps. The heavens, the earth, and in the same breath, the fact that people speak differently and look different. Human variety sits on the same shelf as the sky. Not a problem to solve, and not a ranking: a sign, an aya, the same word used for a verse of the Qur'an. Who is meant to read this sign? Men of knowledge, in Pickthall's English; in Arabic, al-'alimin, those who know. As if the more you learn about people, the more there is to see. Surah Al-Hujurat says something close: We made you nations and tribes so that you might know one another, and the noblest of you with God is the most mindful of Him. And in his farewell pilgrimage sermon, reported in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said an Arab has no superiority over a non-Arab, nor a non-Arab over an Arab, nor a light-skinned person over a dark-skinned one, nor the reverse, except by taqwa. His first community already looked like that: Bilal from Abyssinia, Salman from Persia, Suhayb, called the Roman. This week ran from Al-Qasas through Al-'Ankabut to Ar-Rum: al-amin, do good as good was done, faith is tested, al-'ankabut, within a few years, love and mercy between. And today, the widest: difference is a sign.
screen: `LANGUAGES AND COLORS BESIDE THE SKY.` · `A SIGN FOR THOSE WHO KNOW.` · `NATIONS AND TRIBES, TO KNOW ONE ANOTHER.` · `NO ARAB OVER NON-ARAB, EXCEPT BY TAQWA.`

segments.voice: Think of someone you see often whose first language isn't yours: a neighbor, a colleague, the person at the corner shop, a classmate's parent. Wonder for a moment what they speak at home, and how they'd say hello or thank you in it. If you pray, you can thank God for one person whose difference has taught you something.
Aya. A sign, the same word used for a verse of the Qur'an: what Ar-Rum calls the variety of human languages and colors, beside the heavens and the earth. Today's word.
Your line: difference is a sign. Variety is something to read, not to rank. That's the week.

howItsDone: Muslims often cite 30:22, 49:13 and the Prophet's farewell sermon to teach that no language, people or color is above another, and that only taqwa distinguishes people before God.

chat.says: Does the Qur'an see different languages and skin colors as a problem?
options: No. Ar-Rum lists them among God's signs, beside the heavens and the earth.
It doesn't mention them; it only speaks of believers and unbelievers.
It sees them as differences to be erased in one shared culture.
